result.answer: This case doesn't name a system that holds the patient's history of record. Here is what it does show. The site has set up the receiving system, the demo bed-management system (Downstream Out), as a "current state" system. That means it only needs to know where the patient is now, not every move they made. Its record shows the admission to WARD-A and then the transfer to WARD-C at 09:45 UTC. The failed transfer to WARD-B at 09:20 UTC is missing. The PAS, which sent the messages, recorded the WARD-B move. Shutter can't tell from this case whether any other system keeps the full movement history. Because the patient is already shown on WARD-C, Shutter closed the case as overtaken and sent nothing. If the site marked this receiver as a history-of-record system instead, a case like this would go to a person. Fixing it would mean undoing the later transfer and replaying both in order. That setting isn't in place now (W1).

- `question`: what they asked, and whether it was one of the suggested questions or their own words. It is data.

1. Read the question and the earlier turns. Answer that question, not a summary of everything.
